Surah al-A'raf (Chapter 7)

[Meccan, except from verse 163 up to verse 170, which are Medinan. Its number of verses is 205 or 206. It was revealed after Surah Sad.]

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad.﴾ God knows best what He means by this.

This is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿A Book that has been revealed to you﴾. ﴿So let there be no constriction in your breast about it﴾, meaning narrowness (ḍīq) ﴿concerning it﴾, that you would convey it out of fear that you would be denied. ﴿That you may warn by it﴾: لِتُنْذِر is *mutaʿallaq* (grammatically dependent, i.e., attached to its governing word) on أُنْزِلَ, meaning "for the purpose of warning" (لِلْإنْذارِ). ﴿And a reminder﴾, a reminder (تَذْكِرَة) ﴿for the believers﴾ in it.

Say to them: "Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord," that is, the Qur'an, "and do not follow" (do not take) "other than Him" (that is, other than God) "as protectors" whom you obey in disobedience to Him, the Exalted. "Little do you take heed," with the letter ta' or ya' (you are admonished). In it the ta' of the original form (tatadhakkarun) is assimilated into the dhal, and in another reading it is recited with the ta' sukun (tadhakkarun). The word "ma" is redundant, serving to emphasize the paucity.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 7, verse 4:

﴿And how many a town We have destroyed!﴾ "Kam" (how many) is a khabariyyah (declarative) and is the object (maf'ul) [of the verb implied]. ﴿From a town﴾, meaning its people. ﴿We have destroyed it﴾, meaning We intended to destroy it. ﴿Then Our punishment came upon it﴾, meaning Our chastisement, ﴿by night﴾, meaning at night, ﴿or while they were taking their midday rest﴾, meaning sleeping at midday. Al-qaylulah (the midday rest) is the resting at the middle of the day, even if no sleep accompanies it. That is, [Our punishment] came upon it once at night and once in the daytime.

﴿فَمَا كَانَ دَعْوَاهُمْ﴾ قَوْلَهُمْ

Note: The passage is a short fragment of the commentary, and I have rendered it as given, keeping the Qur'anic quotation and the commentary text.

Translation:

﴿So what was their claim﴾ was their saying

Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, [namely] the nations, about how they responded to the messengers and what they did with what was conveyed to them, ﴿and We will surely question the messengers﴾ about the conveying [of the message].

Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge ﴿فَلَنَقُصَّنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ بِعِلْمٍ﴾, meaning: We will surely inform them, with knowledge of what they did ﴿بِما فَعَلُوهُ﴾. ﴿وما كُنّا غائِبِينَ﴾ means: and We were never absent from conveying the messengers and the earlier nations concerning what they did.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 8:

﴿And the weighing﴾ of the deeds, or of their records, will be by a scale that has a tongue and two pans, as is related in a hadith that exists. ﴿On that Day﴾, meaning the Day of the questioning mentioned, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the truth﴾, meaning the justice, is the attribute of the weighing. ﴿As for those whose scales are heavy﴾ with good deeds, ﴿those are the successful﴾, meaning the winners.
And whoever's scales are light, [that is,] by evil deeds, those are the ones who have lost their souls, [by] consigning them to the Fire, because they were wronging Our signs, [i.e.,] denying them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 10:

﴿And We had certainly established you﴾ O children of Adam, ﴿upon the earth and made for you therein means of livelihood﴾ (with the hamza written as a yā’, i.e., maʿāyish), causes by which you live, the plural of maʿīshah, ﴿little are you grateful﴾ (qalīlan mā), where mā is for emphasizing the paucity, ﴿for that⁠﴾ (i.e., for these blessings).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 7, verse 11:

﴿And We created you﴾, i.e., your father Adam, ﴿then We fashioned you﴾, i.e., We fashioned him while you were in his loins, ﴿then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam."﴾ A prostration of greeting (taḥiyya) by bowing, ﴿so they prostrated, except Iblis﴾, the father of the jinn, who was among the angels.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿What prevented you from﴾ "an lā" (أنْ لا): the لا here is extra (zāʾidah, a redundant particle) ﴿prostrating when﴾ "ḥīn" (حِين), meaning "at the time when."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 13:

﴿He said, "Then descend from it"﴾, i.e., from the Garden. It was also said: from the heavens. ﴿It is not for you to be arrogant therein, so get out﴾ of it, ﴿for you are of the debased﴾, the humiliated.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 14:

﴿He said: "Reprieve me"﴾ (i.e., delay me) ﴿until the day they are raised﴾ (i.e., the people)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 15:

﴿He said: "Indeed you are among those given respite."﴾ And in another verse: ﴿until the Day of the appointed time﴾, meaning the Day of the first blast (of the Trumpet).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 16:

﴿He said: "Because You have led me astray"﴾ i.e., because of Your leading me astray; the "ba'" (bi-, "because of") is for oath, and its answer is ﴿I will surely sit in ambush for them﴾, i.e., for the children of Adam, ﴿on Your straight path﴾, i.e., on the road that leads to You.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 17:

﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left﴾ i.e., from every direction, so that I may bar them from following Your path. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He cannot come at them from above, lest he come between the servant and the mercy of Allah, the Exalted." ﴿And You will not find most of them grateful﴾, i.e., believing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 18:

﴿He said: "Go forth from it, disgraced and expelled."﴾ With a hamza (read as "mad'u'man," i.e., with the hamza), meaning blamed or despised. ﴿Expelled﴾ meaning removed far away from mercy. ﴿Whoever follows you among them﴾ from among mankind. The lam is either for emphasis (lil-ibtida') or introduces an oath (muwatti'a lil-qasam), and the oath is ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you all together﴾, i.e., with you and your offspring and with mankind. In it there is the dominance of the addressed over the absent (taghlib al-hadir 'ala al-ghaib). In the sentence there is also the meaning of a conditional response (jaza') from the conditional particle "man," i.e., whoever follows you, I will punish him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 19:

﴿And﴾ He said, ﴿"O Adam, dwell, you﴾ — a emphasis on the pronoun in "dwell" so that it may be coordinated with it — ﴿and your wife﴾ Hawwa' (Eve), with the long vowel ﴿in Paradise. Eat from wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree﴾ by eating from it, and it is the wheat.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 7, verse 20:

﴿Then Satan whispered to them﴾ Iblis, ﴿in order to reveal to them﴾ to make manifest to them, ﴿what was concealed from them﴾ fa'ala from al-muwara (concealment), ﴿of their private parts﴾, ﴿and said: "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, lest you become angels﴾ out of dislike that you become angels, ﴿or become of the immortals"﴾ (a reading with kasra on the lam is also recorded), ﴿"or become of the immortals."﴾ That is, this (the becoming angels or immortals) is a necessary consequence of eating from it, as in another verse: ﴿"Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn** (the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 7, verse 21:

﴿And he swore to them both﴾, that is, he swore to them by Allah, ﴿"Indeed, I am to you both of the sincere advisors"﴾ in that matter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 22:

﴿So he made them fall⌉ — he brought them down from their station ﴿by deception﴾ from him. ﴿And when they tasted the tree⌉ — i.e., ate from it ﴿their private parts became apparent to them⌉ — i.e., there became manifest to each of them his own private part and the other's private part, and their rear parts. Each of these was called a ﻿sawʼa (private part, that which causes shame) because its exposure distresses its owner. ﴿And they began to join together⌉ — they began to stick ﴿over themselves from the leaves of the Garden⌉ — in order to cover themselves with it. ﴿And their Lord called out to them: Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is a clear enemy to you?﴾ — the interrogative is for affirmation (taqrir).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 23:

﴿They both said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves"﴾ by our disobedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 24:

﴿He said: "Go down"﴾ i.e., Adam and Hawwa', along with what your offspring that you both contain, ﴿some of you﴾ some of the offspring ﴿will be enemies to others﴾ through some of them wronging others. ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place﴾ i.e., a place of settlement, ﴿and provision﴾ enjoyment ﴿for a time﴾ in which your lifespans will come to an end.

﴿He said: "Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth."﴾ — i.e., the earth. "You will live" (taḥyawna), "you will die" (tamūtūna), and "you will be brought forth" (tukhrajūna) by the Resurrection (al-baʿth). The verbs are read in the active and the passive voice (bi-l-binā' lil-fāʿil wal-maf'ūl).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 26:

﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing﴾ meaning, We created it for you, ﴿to cover﴾ conceal ﴿your private parts, and as adornment﴾ and it is what one adorns oneself with of garments, ﴿and the clothing of piety﴾ righteous deeds and good bearing. It is in the accusative (naṣb), being conjoined (ʿaṭf) to "clothing" (libās) in the first clause; and in the nominative (rafʿ) it is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate (khabar) is the following clause, ﴿that is best﴾ ﴿that is among the signs of Allah﴾ the proofs of His power, ﴿so that they may remember﴾ and thus believe. In this there is a shift (iltifāt) from address (khiṭāb) to third person.

O Children of Adam, let not Satan seduce you (yudillannakum, i.e., lead you astray) as he expelled your two parents from the Garden, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts. Indeed, he and his host (qabilah, i.e., his troops) see you from where you do not see them. Indeed, We made the devils allies (awliya', i.e., helpers and companions) for those who do not believe.

When they commit an indecency, such as associating partners with God and circling the House naked, saying, "We do not circle it in clothes in which we have disobeyed God," and they were forbidden this, ﴿they say: "We found our fathers doing it, and God has commanded us to do it."﴾ So we follow them in it, and ﴿God has commanded us to do it﴾ too. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"Indeed God does not command indecency. Do you say about God what you do not know?"﴾ That he said it: this is an interrogative of denial (istifham inkar).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 29:

﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice (bil-qist)﴾ bil-ʿadl (with justice, equity).

﴿And set your faces upright﴾ is coordinated (maʿtuf) upon the meaning of "bil-qist" — that is, "He said: Be just and set upright" — or, the verb before it is an implied "fa-aqbilū" (so turn), i.e. ﴿your faces﴾ toward Allah ﴿at every place of worship﴾, meaning: make your prostrations sincerely for Him. ﴿And call upon Him﴾, meaning worship Him, ﴿making your religion sincere for Him﴾, away from shirk. ﴿As He originated you﴾, created you when you were nothing, ﴿so you will return﴾, meaning He will restore you alive on the Day of Resurrection.
﴿A group﴾ of you ﴿He guided, and a group upon whom error was justly decreed. Indeed, they took the devils as allies instead of Allah﴾, i.e., other than Him.

O Children of Adam, take your adornment: what covers your nakedness, at every place of prayer (ʿinda kulli masjid), meaning at the time of prayer and circumambulation (al-ṭawāf), and eat and drink whatever you wish.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 32:

﴿Say﴾ in rebuke of them: ﴿"Who has forbidden the adornment of God, which He has brought forth for His servants,"﴾ of clothing, ﴿"and the good things"﴾ the delicious things ﴿"of provision?" Say﴾ ﴿"They are for those who believed in the life of this world,"﴾ by right, even if others share them with them, ﴿"purely"﴾ exclusively for them, in the nominative or accusative (as a circumstantial state, ḥāl) ﴿"on the Day of Resurrection. Thus do We detail the signs"﴾ We make them clear, with this same detail ﴿"for a people who know"﴾ who reflect, for they are the ones who benefit from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 33:

﴿Say: "My Lord has only forbidden the great sins (al-fawahish), such as fornication, those of them that are apparent and those that are concealed,﴾ and the sin (al-ithm), meaning disobedience, and transgression (al-baghy) against people ﴿without right﴾, which is injustice, ﴿and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾, meaning by your associating [others with Him], ﴿and that you say about Allah what you do not know﴾ of forbidding what He has not forbidden, and other things.﴾
For every nation there is a term (ajal), a set period. When their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it.

O Children of Adam! If there come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses, then whoever fears God (attaqa) and does good (aslaha), there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve.

**Translation:**

﴿O Children of Adam! If there come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses⦆ — here the nūn of the conditional particle in (إنْ) is assimilated into the extra (zā'idah) mā (ما), so the reading is "imma" (إمّا).

﴿Then whoever fears (attaqā)﴾ — i.e., fears shirk (al-shirk, associating partners with God), ﴿and does righteous deeds (aṣlaḥa)﴾ — i.e., his deed, ﴿there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve﴾ — in the Hereafter.
And those who denied Our signs and waxed proud against them (they became arrogant towards them), and so did not believe in them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 37:

﴿Who₍fa-man₎﴾ i.e., there is no one ﴿more unjust than he who fabricates against Allah a lie﴾ by attributing to Him a partner and a son ﴿or denies His signs﴾, the Qur'an. ﴿Those will receive their share﴾, that is, what is destined for them ﴿of the Decree﴾ (al-kitab), meaning what has been written for them in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz) of provision, term of life, and other things ﴿until when Our messengers come to them, taking them in death﴾, i.e., the angels, ﴿they will say﴾ to them, rebuking them, ﴿"Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?"﴾, that is, worship. ﴿They will say, "They have gone astray from us"﴾, i.e., vanished, ﴿so we do not see them,﴾ ﴿and they will testify against themselves﴾ at the time of death.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 38:

﴿He said﴾ — Exalted is He — to them on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Enter into﴾ the company of ﴿nations that have passed away before you, of jinn and mankind, into the Fire﴾ — this is connected to "enter." ﴿Every time a nation enters﴾ the Fire ﴿it curses its sister﴾ — the one before it — ﴿for having misled it﴾ ﴿until, when they have all overtaken one another therein﴾ — that is, have followed one another — ﴿the last of them will say to the first of them﴾ — and they are the followers — ﴿Meaning, to their leaders, and they are those who were followed﴾ ﴿Our Lord, these have led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire﴾ — doubling it. ﴿He said﴾ — Exalted is He — ﴿To each of you﴾ and to them ﴿is a double﴾ punishment, a doubled punishment. ﴿But you do not know﴾ — read with the ya' and with the ta' — what is due to each group.
﴿The first of them will say to the last of them: "You had no superiority over us."﴾ Because you did not disbelieve because of us, so we and you are equal.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them﴾ (takabbaru ʿanha, they behaved arrogantly toward them) ﴿and so did not believe in them﴾, ﴿the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾ when their spirits are raised up to it after death, so they are sent down to Sijjin (a place of the wicked), unlike the believer, for whom it is opened and his spirit is taken up to the seventh heaven, as is reported in a hadith. ﴿Nor will they enter the Garden until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾ (yalij, enters; thuqb al-ibra, the eye of the needle), which is impossible, and likewise their entry (into the Garden is impossible). ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminals﴾ with disbelief.

For them there will be a bed of Hellfire beneath them (mihad: firash, a bedding/spread), and above them coverings (ghawashin: aghta'iya, coverings) of fire. It is the plural of ghashiya, and its tanwin is a substitute (iwad) for the omitted yaa'.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is the subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject of a nominal sentence) ﴿We do not charge any soul except [according to] its capacity﴾, meaning its ability in terms of deeds, is a parenthetical insertion (i'tiraḍ, a phrase placed between two parts of a sentence) between it and its predicate, which is: ﴿those are the companions of the Garden﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 43:

﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾, i.e., rancor (ḥiqd) that was between them in the world. ﴿Rivers will flow beneath them﴾, i.e., beneath their palaces. ﴿The rivers.﴾ ﴿And they will say﴾ upon settling in their abodes: ﴿"All praise is due to Allah, who has guided us to this﴾, i.e., to the deed whose reward this is. ﴿And we would never have been guided if it had not been that Allah guided us."﴾ The response to lawla (“if it had not been for”) is omitted, because what precedes it indicates it. ﴿Certainly the messengers of our Lord came with the truth." And they will be called, "That﴾ is a lightened form (mukhaffafah), i.e., that it (innahu), or an explanatory form (mufassirah) in the five places.

And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire, [to affirm and to rebuke]: "We have found what our Lord promised us to be true," [meaning the reward]. "Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?" [meaning the punishment]. They will say, "Yes." Then a caller will proclaim between them, [between the two groups, making them hear]:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 45:

﴿Those who bar﴾ people ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, His religion, ﴿and seek to make it crooked﴾, i.e., they seek for the way to be ﴿crooked﴾, deviating.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 7, verse 46:**

﴿And between them⦆ i.e., the people of the Garden and the Fire, ﴿is a barrier⦆, a partition. It was said that it is the wall of al-A'raf (the Heights), ﴿and upon the A'raf⦆, which is the wall of the Garden, ﴿are men⦆ whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, as in the hadith. ﴿They recognize each of them⦆ among the people of the Garden and the Fire ﴿by their marks⦆, i.e., by their signs, which are the whiteness of the faces for the believers and the blackness of the faces for the disbelievers, because they see them, since their position is elevated. ﴿They have not entered it⦆, i.e., the people of al-A'raf have not entered the Garden, ﴿but they hope⦆ to enter it. Al-Hasan said: "He has not made them hope except for an honour He intends for them." Al-Hakim related from Hudhayfah, who said: "While they are like that, your Lord looks down upon them and says: 'Arise and enter the Garden, for I have forgiven you.'"
﴿And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire﴾ — that is, the companions of the Heights (a'raf) — ﴿they say: "Our Lord, do not place us﴾ in the Fire.

﴿And the companions of the Heights (al-A'raf) call out to men﴾ from among the companions of the Fire, ﴿whom they recognize by their marks, saying: "What did your gathering (of wealth) avail you﴾ against the Fire? ﴿Your wealth (jam'kum)﴾, or ﴿your multitude (kathratukum)﴾? ﴿And your arrogance (istikbarukum)﴾, i.e., your arrogance toward faith, ﴿which you used to show.﴾" They say this to them, pointing to the weak among the Muslims.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 49:

﴿Are these the ones of whom you swore that Allah would not grant them mercy?﴾ [It has been said to them]: ﴿Enter the Garden; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve.﴾ It is also read: ۤ"Udkhilū" (أُدْخِلُوا) with the passive voice (bi-l-bina' li-l-maf'ul), and "dakhalū" (دَخَلُوا). The negative clause (fa-jumlat al-nafy) is then a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: being told this (maqūlan lahum dhalik).

The Companions of the Fire will call out to the Companions of the Garden: "Pour some water over us, or some of the provision God has provided you," [meaning] of food. They will reply: "God has forbidden both of them," [meaning] He has withheld them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 51:

﴿Those who took their religion as amusement and play, and whom the worldly life deceived.﴾ Then today We will forget them, i.e., leave them in the Fire, ﴿as they forgot the meeting of this their Day﴾ by abandoning action for it, ﴿and as they used to deny Our signs.﴾ I.e., just as they denied them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 52:

﴿And We have certainly brought them a Book﴾ i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿a Book﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿which We have detailed﴾ We have clarified it with reports, promise and threat, ﴿with knowledge﴾ a circumstantial clause, i.e., knowing what He has detailed in it, ﴿as guidance﴾ a circumstantial clause from the pronoun (in "detailed it"), ﴿and mercy for a people who believe﴾ in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 53:

﴿Do they await anything but its fulfilment?﴾ That is, what are they waiting for, other than its consequence, which is in it (ma fihi)? ﴿On the day its fulfilment comes﴾ it is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Those who had forgotten it before will say﴾ they had abandoned belief in it. ﴿Indeed the messengers of our Lord came with the truth. Do we have any intercessors who might intercede for us, or can we be sent back﴾ to the world ﴿so that we may do other than what we used to do?﴾ that we would affirm the oneness of God and abandon polytheism. It will be said to them: No. ﴿They have lost their souls﴾ in that they have come to ruin. ﴿And what they used to invent has gone astray from them﴾ departed (dhahaba), namely the claim of partners.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 54:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾ of the days of this world, meaning in their measure, because there was no sun then. Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 55:

﴿Call upon your Lord humbly﴾, [tadarru'an is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the action)], meaning in submissiveness (tadhallul), ﴿and secretly﴾, meaning privately. ﴿Indeed, He does not love the transgressors﴾, in supplication, through exaggerated affectation of speech (al-tashaddug) and raising the voice.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 56:

﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order﴾ by associating partners with Allah and by sins, ﴿after its reformation﴾ by the sending of the messengers. ﴿And call upon Him in fear﴾ of His punishment ﴿and in hope﴾ of His mercy. ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good﴾ who are obedient. Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 57:

﴿And He is the One who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾, meaning scattered (mutafarriqah) ahead of the rain. In another reading the shin is made sukun for lightness (takhfif); in another it is sukun with the nun fatha as a verbal noun (masdar); and in another it is sukun with the ba' (waw) damma in place of the nun: i.e., bringing good tidings (mubashshiran). Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 58:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 69:

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 7, verse 71:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 72:

﴿So We delivered him﴾, that is, Hud, ﴿and those who were with him﴾ of the believers, ﴿by a mercy from Us. And We cut off the last remnant﴾ of the people ﴿who denied Our signs﴾, that is, We uprooted them, ﴿and they were not believers﴾, a conjunction with ﴿denied﴾.

﴿And﴾ We sent ﴿to Thamud﴾ — read without tanwin, intending by it the tribe — ﴿their brother Salih. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 74:

﴿And remember when He made you successors﴾ in the earth ﴿after the people of ʿAd and settled you﴾ made you dwell ﴿in the earth, taking from its plains palaces﴾ which you dwell in during the summer ﴿and hewing out the mountains as houses﴾ which you dwell in during the winter. It is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl muqaddara), meaning "intending to take," i.e., the taking and hewing are to be understood as something that will occur later.

﴿The chiefs of his people who were arrogant said﴾: they were arrogant about believing in him. ﴿To those who were oppressed, to those among them who believed﴾: i.e., among his people. It is a *badal* (substitution, or apposition) for what precedes it, with the preposition repeated (*bi-i'adat al-jar*). ﴿Do you know that Salih is one sent from his Lord?﴾ to you. ﴿They said﴾: "Yes."

The camel had a day for drinking water and they had a day, but they grew weary of that. ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel﴾ Qudar hamstrung her at their command, by killing her with the sword. ﴿And they defied the command of their Lord, and said: O Salih, bring upon us what you threaten us with﴾ of punishment, over her killing.
﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾: a violent quaking from the earth and a shout from the sky. ﴿So they became, in their homes, prostrate on their knees﴾, dead.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 81:

﴿ A-innakum﴾ with the two hamzas pronounced (both realised as hamza), the second one made easy (tashil), and an alif inserted between them, in both ways of reading; and in another reading, ﴿innakum﴾ (without the interrogative hamza). ﴿La-ta'tūna al-rijāl shahwatan min dūn al-nisā'? Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 82:

﴿And the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel them from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."﴾ That is, Lut and his followers. ﴿From your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ from the anuses of men.
﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind.﴾ [That is,] those who remained behind in the punishment.
And We rained upon them a rain (of stones). ﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾: it was the stones of sijjil, and it destroyed them.

And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. There has certainly come to you a clear proof (bayyinah) from your Lord" — a miracle (mu'jizah) testifying to my truthfulness. Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 86:

﴿And do not sit on every path﴾ road, ﴿threatening﴾ frightening the people by taking their garments or the illicit toll (al-maks) from them, ﴿and barring﴾ turning away ﴿from the way of Allah﴾ His religion ﴿those who believe in Him﴾ by your threatening them with killing, ﴿and seeking to make it crooked﴾ seeking the road to be ﴿crooked﴾ deviant. ﴿And remember when you were few, and He multiplied you. And look at how was the end of the corrupters﴾ before you, through their denial of their messengers; i.e., the final outcome of their affair was destruction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 87:

﴿And if there is a group among you who has believed in that with which I have been sent, and a group who has not believed,﴾ [in it] ﴿then be patient﴾ wait ﴿until Allah judges between us﴾ and you, by saving the one who is right and destroying the one who is wrong. ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾, the most just of them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 88:

﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said﴾ (against faith): ﴿"We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you from our town, or you will return﴾ (tarji'un, you will go back) ﴿to our religion"﴾ (dinina, our religion). They used the plural in address for the singular, because Shu'ayb had never been in their religion at all; and he answered in a similar manner. ﴿He said﴾ (We will return to it) ﴿"Even though we were unwilling?"﴾ (awa-law kunna karihin, the interrogative here is one of denial, meaning: we would not return even if we were unwilling).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 89:

﴿We have indeed fabricated a lie against Allah if we return to your religion after Allah has rescued us from it. It is not for us to return to it, unless Allah, our Lord, should will it.﴾ That is, He would forsake us. ﴿Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge﴾ That is, His knowledge encompasses all things, including my state and yours. ﴿In Allah we have put our trust. Our Lord, decide﴾ judge ﴿between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who decide﴾ the judges.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 90:

﴿And the chiefs of those among his people who disbelieved said﴾, i.e., some of them said to others, ﴿"If﴾ — the lam is a lam of oath.
﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾ the severe quake, ﴿and they became in their abode prostrate﴾ kneeling on their knees, dead.

﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb﴾ is a *mubtada'* (subject of a nominal sentence), whose *khabar* (predicate) is ﴿*ka'anna*﴾ (as if), in its lightened form (*mukhaffafa*), with its noun omitted. The implied noun is *ka'annahum* (as if they). ﴿Had not dwelt﴾ means ﴿*lam yaghnaw*﴾, that is, *yuqimu* (lived or stayed). ﴿Therein﴾ means ﴿*fihā*﴾, that is, *fī diyarihim* (in their homes). ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb, it was they who were the losers﴾. The emphasis, through repeating the relative pronoun and the other elements, serves as a refutation of them in their earlier statement.

﴿So he turned away from them﴾ and said, "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you sincerely," [but you did not believe]. ﴿So how should I grieve over a people who are disbelievers?﴾ (آسى) means "I grieve" or "I am sad" (أحزن). The interrogative form is used in the sense of negation (استفهام بمعنى النفي), meaning: I do not grieve over a disbelieving people.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 94:

﴿And We did not send into any city a prophet﴾ and they denied him, ﴿except that We seized﴾ (We punished) ﴿its people with adversity﴾ (severity of poverty) ﴿and affliction﴾ (sickness), ﴿that they might humble themselves﴾ (abase themselves) ﴿and so believe﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 95:

﴿Then We replaced﴾ We gave them ﴿in place of the evil﴾ the punishment ﴿the good﴾ wealth and health, ﴿until they multiplied﴾ they grew in number, ﴿and said﴾ in ingratitude for the blessing, ﴿Indeed, adversity and ease have touched our fathers﴾ as they have touched us, and this is the custom of time, and it is not a punishment from God, so remain as you are, ﴿then We seized them﴾ with the punishment ﴿suddenly﴾ unexpectedly, ﴿while they did not perceive﴾ the time of its coming before it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 96:

﴿And if the people of the towns had believed﴾ (who denied the messengers) ﴿and had been mindful of God﴾ (by abandoning disbelief and sins), ﴿We would have opened up for them blessings from the heaven﴾ (with rain) ﴿and the earth﴾ (with plants). ﴿But they denied﴾ the messengers, ﴿so We seized them﴾ (We punished them) for what they earned.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah al-A'raf (7), verse 97:

﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure﴾ (that is, the deniers) ﴿that Our might (ba's) will come upon them﴾ (that is, Our punishment) ﴿by night﴾ (that is, at night) ﴿while they are asleep﴾ (that is, heedless of it).

(Tafsir al-Jalalayn): duha: in daytime (nahaaran).
﴿Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah?﴾ [That is] His gradual leading of them on (istidraj) by means of blessings, and His seizing them suddenly.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 100:

﴿Has it not become clear⁠﻿ to those who inherit the earth⁠﻿ through dwelling in it after the destruction of its people⁠﻿ that⁠﻿ (an) (here "that" is the lightened form of "inna", with its noun omitted, meaning: that it) ﴿if We willed, We would smite them﴾ with punishment ﴿for their sins﴾, as We smote those before them? The hamza in the four places is for rebuke, and the fa and waw that precede them are for coordination. In one reading, the waw in the first place is vowelled with sukun, as a coordination by "aw" (or). ﴿And We seal﴾ (i.e. We lock) ﴿their hearts, so they do not hear﴾ the admonition with the hearing of reflection.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 101:

﴿Those were the cities﴾ whose account has already been mentioned, ﴿We relate to you﴾ O Muhammad ﴿some of their news﴾, the reports of their people. ﴿And their messengers had certainly come to them with the clear proofs﴾, the evident miracles, ﴿but they were not to believe﴾ when they came ﴿in what they had denied﴾, i.e., disbelieved in it, ﴿before﴾ the time of their coming; rather, they persisted in disbelief. ﴿Thus﴾ (is) the sealing (of hearts), ﴿the sealing﴾

﴿And We found not for most of them﴾, i.e., the people, ﴿any covenant﴾, i.e., fulfilment of their covenant, on the day the covenant was taken. ﴿And indeed﴾ — ﴿وإنْ﴾ is *mukhaffafa* (a lightened form of *inna*).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 103:

﴿Then after them We sent Moses﴾ i.e., the messengers mentioned, ﴿with Our signs﴾ the nine (signs), ﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ his people, ﴿but they wronged them﴾ i.e., they disbelieved in them. ﴿So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾ through disbelief, [i.e., see] their destruction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 104:

﴿And Musa said, "O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds"﴾ to you, but he denied him.

Worthy [of] ﴿that﴾, i.e., it is fitting for me ﴿not to say about Allah except the truth﴾. In another reading, the yā' is doubled [ḥaqqīq], so ḥaqīq is the subject (mubtada') and its predicate (khabar) is "an" and what follows it. ﴿I have certainly come to you with a clear sign from your Lord, so send with me﴾ to al-Shām (Syria) ﴿the Children of Israel﴾, whom [Pharaoh] had enslaved.
﴿He [Pharaoh] said﴾ to him (Moses), ﴿"If you have come with a sign"﴾ as evidence for your claim, ﴿"then produce it, if you are among the truthful"﴾ in it.
﴿So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a serpent, plainly visible.﴾ A great serpent.

﴿And he drew out his hand﴾ he brought it out from his collar, ﴿and behold, it was white﴾ possessing radiance, ﴿to the onlookers﴾, contrary to what it had been of brownness (*udmah*, a darker, wheaten complexion).

﴿The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said: "Indeed, this is a knowing magician."﴾ [Excelling in knowledge of magic.] In Surat al-Shu'ara' (it is said) that it was from Pharaoh's own words, so it was as if they said it along with him, by way of consultation.
﴿They said: "Put them off, him and his brother"﴾, that is, delay their matter, ﴿and send into the cities gatherers﴾, that is, collectors.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 112:

﴿They will bring you every skilled sorcerer﴾, and in another reading (qira'a) "sahhar" (a more intensive form of "sahir") ﴿knowing﴾, surpassing Musa in knowledge of magic (sihr). So they gathered [the sorcerers].

﴿And the magicians came to Pharaoh; they said, "Indeed..."﴾ with both hamzahs (the glottal stop, ء) pronounced in full (tahqiq, "realization"), and the second hamzah softened (tashil, "easing"), and an alif inserted between them, in both ways of reading.

They said, "O Musa, either you throw, or we become the throwers," meaning: what is with us.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 116:
