Pharaoh said: "Have you believed in him before I give you permission? Indeed, this is a plot you have plotted in the city, to expel its people from it. But you will come to know."

Note on the passage:

- ﴿آمَنتُمْ﴾ ("Have you believed") is recited with the two hamzas pronounced as separate hamzas, the second being changed to an alif (بِتَحْقِيقِ الهَمْزَتَيْنِ وإبْدال الثّانِيَة ألِفًا). This is a point of recitation (tajwid) and does not change the meaning.
- ﴿بِهِ﴾ ("in him") refers to Musa (ʿalayhi al-salām).
- ﴿أنا﴾ ("I") is the subject of the verb ﴿آذَنَ﴾ ("give permission"), expressed as the implied subject that the commentary spells out.
- ﴿لَمَكْر مَكَرْتُمُوهُ﴾ ("a plot you have plotted") refers to what they had done (الَّذِي صَنَعْتُمُوهُ), namely the scheme attributed to Musa and his people in the city.
- ﴿فَسَوْف تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ ("But you will come to know") means you will learn what punishment from me will befall you (ما يَنالكُمْ مِنِّي).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 124:

﴿Surely I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides﴾, i.e., the right hand of each one and the left foot.
They said, "Indeed we are to our Lord" after our death, in whatever manner it may be, "returning" (munqalibun), that is, returning in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 126:

﴿Wa-mā tanqimu﴾ (do you resent / hold against) ﴿minnā illā an āmannā bi-āyāti Rabbinā lammā jāatnā﴾ (except that we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us). ﴿Rabbanā afrigh ʿalaynā ṣabran﴾ (Our Lord, pour upon us patience) at the time of carrying out what You threaten us with, ﴿li-allā narjiʿa kuffāran﴾ (so that we do not revert to disbelievers).

﴿The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said﴾ to him, ﴿"Will you leave﴾ (tatruk, i.e. abandon) ﴿Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land﴾ by calling people to oppose you, ﴿and abandon you and your gods?"﴾ He had made for them small idols which they worshipped, and he said, "I am your lord," and their lord. That is why he said, ﴿"I am your Most High lord"﴾. ﴿He said, "We will kill﴾ (with the shaddah, the doubling of the letter, and with the takhfif, the lightening, i.e. a single consonant, both readings are valid) ﴿their sons﴾ who are born, ﴿and spare﴾ (nastabqi, i.e. keep alive) ﴿their women﴾ as we did to them before, ﴿and indeed we are over them dominant﴾ (qadirun, i.e. capable)." So they did that to them, and the Children of Israel complained.

﴿Musa said to his people: "Seek help from Allah and be patient"﴾ (against) ﴿their harm﴾. ﴿"Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah. He bequeaths it﴾ (gives it) ﴿to whomever He wills of His servants. And the final outcome"﴾ (the praiseworthy one) ﴿"is for the God-fearing﴾" (Allah).

﴿They said, "We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us." He said, "It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and He will see how you act."﴾ fīhā (therein)

﴿And We certainly seized the family of Pharaoh with years﴾ [of drought], ﴿and a shortage of fruits, so that perhaps they would be mindful﴾, i.e., with famine (bi-l-qahṭ), ﴿and a shortage of fruits﴾, ﴿so that perhaps they would be mindful﴾, i.e., take warning (yatta'iẓūn), ﴿so that they would believe﴾ (fa-yu'minūn).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 131:

﴿Then when good came to them﴾ abundance and wealth, ﴿they said: "This is ours by right"﴾ i.e., we deserve it, and they did not give thanks for it. ﴿But if evil befell them﴾ drought and calamity, ﴿they ascribed it as an omen﴾ (yatatayyaru, from tiyara, to take omens of ill luck) ﴿to Moses and those with him﴾ of the believers. ﴿Indeed, their omen is with Allah﴾ their misfortune; He brings it upon them. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ that what befalls them is from Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 132:

﴿And they said﴾ to Musa, ﴿"Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will not be believers in you."﴾ So he invoked against them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 133:

﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾, which was water that entered their houses and reached the throats of those sitting, for seven days; ﴿and the locusts﴾, which ate their crops and fruits likewise; ﴿and the lice﴾, the weevil (sus) or a kind of tick, which pursued what the locusts had left; ﴿and the frogs﴾, which filled their houses and their food; ﴿and the blood﴾ in their water; ﴿as distinct signs﴾, clear and explanatory; ﴿but they were arrogant﴾ about believing in them.

﴿And when the punishment fell upon them﴾, the torment, ﴿they said, "O Moses, pray to your Lord for us, by what He has covenanted with you﴾, that He remove the torment from us, ﴿if we believe﴾, ﴿indeed, if﴾ the لام (lām) here is the lām of oath (lām al-qasam), ﴿…﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 135:

﴿So when We removed from them the punishment﴾ by the supplication of Musa, ﴿until a term which they were to reach, behold, they broke their word.﴾ They violated their covenant and persisted in their disbelief.
So We took vengeance on them and drowned them in the sea (al-yamm), the salt sea (al-bahr al-milh), because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them, not reflecting upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 137:

﴿And We caused to inherit the people who had been oppressed﴾ by enslavement, ﴿namely the Children of Israel, the eastern and western parts of the land﴾ (mashariq al-ard wa-magharibaha), ﴿which We had blessed﴾ with water and trees. It is an attribute of "the land," and it is al-Sham (Greater Syria). ﴿And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled﴾ (wa-tammat kalimat Rabbika al-husna), and it is His, the Exalted, statement: ﴿And We wished to show favour to those who were oppressed in the land﴾, etc., ﴿upon the Children of Israel, because they had patience﴾ (bi-ma sabaru) over the harm of their enemy. ﴿And We destroyed﴾ (wa-dammarna), meaning We annihilated, ﴿what Pharaoh and his people had been building﴾ (ma kana yasna'u Fir'awn wa-qawmuhu), from structures, ﴿and what they had been erecting﴾ (wa-ma kanu ya'rishun), with the letter ra' pronounced with kasra and with damma, meaning they were raising up, from buildings.

And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people who were devoted to (ya'kufuna, with the kaf pronounced with a damma or a kasra) idols they had. They said, "O Musa, make for us a god" (ilahan, i.e. an idol we may worship), "just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed you are a people who act in ignorance," in that you have repaid God's blessing upon you with what you have said.
﴿Indeed, these [people]—they are doomed﴾ (هالك), destroyed.

﴿He said, "Should I seek for you a god other than Allah,﴾ worshipped. Its original form is أبْغِي لَكُمْ (abghi lakum, "I seek for you"), ﴿when it is He who has favored you over the worlds﴾ of your time, by what He mentioned in His words

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, a concise commentary, *tafsir*: explanation) on Surah 7, verse 141:**

﴿And﴾ remember ﴿when We delivered you﴾ from the people of Pharaoh ﴿who were subjecting you﴾ to, meaning they were imposing upon you and making you taste ﴿the evil torment﴾, its most severe form. This is when ﴿they slaughtered your sons and spared your women﴾, meaning they were sparing them. ﴿And in that﴾, meaning in the deliverance or in the torment, there is ﴿a trial﴾, meaning a blessing or a test, ﴿from your Lord, a great [one]﴾. Will you not then take heed, so that you cease from what you have said?

In another recitation (*qira'a*, a variant mode of reciting the Qur'an), the word أنَجاكُمْ (*anjākum*, "He delivered you") appears in place of أنْجَيْناكُمْ (*anjaynākum*, "We delivered you").

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah al-A'raf, verse 142:

﴿وواعَدْنا﴾ [We appointed] with one thousand and less, ﴿مُوسى ثَلاثِينَ لَيْلَة﴾ [Musa thirty nights], to speak with him at their end. This was by commanding him to fast them, and they were in Dhu al-Qa'dah. So he fasted them. When they were completed, he noticed a change in the odour of his mouth, so he used a siwak (tooth-stick). Then God commanded him with ten more, so that He might speak with him with the odour of his mouth. ﴿وأَتْمَمْناها بِعَشْرٍ﴾ [And We completed them with ten] from Dhu al-Hijjah. ﴿فَتَمَّ مِيقات رَبّه﴾ [So the appointed time of his Lord was completed], the time of His promise to speak with him, ﴿أرْبَعِينَ﴾ [forty] as a *hal* (circumstantial accusative, the Arabic grammatical term for a state or condition expressed by an accusative noun), ﴿لَيْلَة﴾ [night] as a *tamyiz* (specification accusative, the Arabic grammatical term for a noun clarifying a number). ﴿وقالَ مُوسى لِأَخِيهِ هارُونَ﴾ [And Musa said to his brother Harun] when he went to the mountain for the private conversation, ﴿اُخْلُفْنِي﴾ [be my successor] ﴿فِي قَوْمِي وأَصْلِحْ﴾ [among my people, and set right] their affairs, ﴿ولا تَتَّبِع سَبِيل المُفْسِدِينَ﴾ [and do not follow the way of the corrupters], by agreeing with them in acts of disobedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 143:

﴿And when Musa came at Our appointed time﴾, i.e., at the time which We had promised him that We would speak with him in it, ﴿and his Lord spoke to him﴾ without an intermediary, speech which he heard from every direction, ﴿he said: "My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You." He said: "You will not see Me"﴾, i.e., you are not able to see Me. The expression "You will not see Me" rather than "I will not be seen" indicates the possibility of His being seen, may He be exalted. ﴿But look at the mountain﴾, which is stronger than you, ﴿and if it remains firm in its place﴾, i.e., stays in place, ﴿then you will see Me﴾, i.e., you will be steadfast for My sight; otherwise you have no strength for it. ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain﴾, i.e., appeared from His light the size of the tip of the little finger, as in a hadith authenticated by al-Hakim, ﴿He made it crumble to dust﴾, with the short and the long vowel (dakkan / dakka'an), i.e., leveled and flattened to the ground, ﴿and Musa fell down unconscious﴾, swooned from the terror of what he saw. ﴿And when he recovered, he said: "Glory be to You"﴾, declaring You far above such things, ﴿I have repented to You﴾ for asking what I was not commanded to ask, ﴿and I am the first of the believers﴾ in my time.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 144:

God said to him: ﴿O Moses, I have chosen you﴾ over ﴿mankind﴾, meaning the people of your time, ﴿by My messages﴾, read with the plural and with the singular, ﴿and by My speaking﴾, meaning My speaking to you. ﴿So take what I have given you﴾ of the favour, ﴿and be among the thankful﴾ for My blessings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 145:

﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets﴾ i.e., the tablets of the Torah, and they were made of sidr of Paradise, or of chrysolite (zabarjad), or of emerald (zumurrud), seven or ten in number. ﴿Of everything﴾ that is needed in the religion, ﴿an admonition and a detailed explanation﴾ (tafsil), a clarification ﴿of everything﴾. (This phrase is) a substitute (badal) for the prepositional phrase preceding it. ﴿So take hold of them﴾, with the implied (muqaddar) word before it, "We said," ﴿with strength﴾, with earnestness and striving, ﴿and enjoin your people to take the best of them. I shall show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqin)﴾, the abode of Pharaoh and his followers, which is Egypt, so that you may take warning from them.

﴿I will turn away from My signs﴾ the proofs of My power, from created things and other than them, ﴿those who are arrogant in the earth without right﴾ by forsaking them so that they are not arrogant therein. ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it; and if they see the way of right guidance﴾ the path, the guidance that came from Allah, ﴿they will not take it as a way﴾ they will not travel it. ﴿And if they see the way of error﴾ misguidance, ﴿they will take it as a way. That﴾ the turning away ﴿is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾ a similar explanation has already been given.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 7, verse 147:

﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾ — the resurrection and other things — ﴿their deeds have become worthless﴾ — they have been nullified — ﴿what they did﴾ of good in the world, such as maintaining family ties and giving charity, so there is no reward for them because the condition for it is absent. ﴿Are they recompensed except﴾ with the recompense of ﴿what they used to do﴾ of denial and sins?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 148:

﴿And the people of Musa took, after him,﴾ meaning after his departure to the place of intimate conversation (munājāh), ﴿from their ornaments,﴾ which they had borrowed from the people of Firʿawn on the pretext of a wedding feast, and so it remained with them, ﴿a calf﴾ which al-Sāmirī fashioned for them from it, ﴿a body﴾ that was transformed into flesh and blood, ﴿which had a lowing﴾ meaning a sound that could be heard. It was transformed in this way by placing in it the dust that he had taken from the hoofprint of Jibrīl's horse in his fist, for its effect is that life comes to whatever it is placed in. The second object (maf'ūl thānī) of "took" (ittakhadha) is omitted, meaning "as a god." ﴿Did they not see that it does not speak to them, nor guide them to a way?﴾ So how could it be taken as a god? ﴿They took it﴾ as a god, ﴿and they were wrongdoers﴾ by taking it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 149:

﴿And when they were overcome with regret﴾ i.e., they repented of their worship (of the calf), ﴿and saw﴾ i.e., knew, ﴿that they had gone astray﴾ by it, and this was after Musa's return, ﴿they said: "If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us"﴾ with the ya' and the ta' (i.e., both verbs may be read with ya' or ta' at the beginning)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 150:

﴿When Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved⁠—﴾ angry at them ﴿and deeply saddened⁠—﴾ ﴿he said: "Evil is what you have done as my successors after me!"⁠﴾ meaning: evil is the succession you have carried out in my place, your succession to me, since you have associated others with God. ﴿"Have you hastened the command of your Lord?"⁠﴾ ﴿And he threw down the Tablets⁠﴾ the Tablets of the Torah, out of zeal for his Lord, so that they broke. ﴿And he seized his brother by the head⁠﴾ meaning by his hair, with his right hand, and by his beard with his left ﴿dragging him towards himself⁠﴾ in anger. ﴿He said⁠﴾ ﴿"O son of my mother!"⁠﴾ — the word for "mother" may be read with a kasra or a fatha on the mim; he meant "my mother," and mentioning her was more tender to his heart. ﴿"Indeed the people have deemed me weak and were close to killing me, so do not let the enemies rejoice over me⁠﴾ at your humiliating me ﴿and do not place me with the wrongdoing people⁠﴾ in the worship of the calf, so that I am held to account with them.
﴿He said, "My Lord, forgive me"﴾ for what I did to my brother, ﴿and my brother﴾, whom I include in the supplication, to please him and to ward off the gloating of others over him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 152:

﴿Indeed, those who took the calf﴾ as a god ﴿will be overtaken by anger﴾, i.e., punishment, ﴿from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world﴾. So they were punished by the command to kill themselves, and humiliation was struck upon them until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And thus﴾, just as We recompensed them, ﴿We recompense those who fabricate﴾ lies against Allah, by associating partners with Him and other than that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 153:

﴿And those who committed evil deeds and then repented after them and believed﴾ — they turned back from them — ﴿indeed, your Lord, after them﴾ — i.e., after the repentance — ﴿is Forgiving﴾ toward them ﴿and Merciful﴾ toward them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 154:

﴿And when the anger subsided⟩ (sakata) from Musa, ﴿he took up the tablets⟩ which he had thrown down. ﴿And in their inscription⟩, i.e., what was copied (nusikha) in them, i.e., written, ﴿was guidance⟩ from misguidance, ﴿and mercy for those who fear their Lord⟩, i.e., who are afraid of Him. The lam was introduced before the object because it came first.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 155:

﴿And Musa chose from his people﴾, i.e., from among his people, ﴿seventy men﴾ of those who had not worshipped the calf by His command, may He be exalted, ﴿for Our appointed time﴾, i.e., for the time We had promised him to bring them at, so that they might apologize for their companions' worship of the calf. So he set out with them. ﴿Then when the earthquake seized them﴾, i.e., the severe tremor. Ibn ʿAbbas said: this was because they had not separated themselves from their people when they worshipped the calf. He said: and they were not the ones who asked to see God, and those were seized by the thunderbolt. ﴿He said﴾, Musa: ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You would have destroyed them before, and me too﴾, i.e., before my departure with them, so that the Children of Israel would witness that and not accuse him. ﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did?﴾ This is a question seeking sympathy, i.e., do not punish us for the sin of others. ﴿It is not﴾, i.e., ﴿except Your trial﴾, i.e., Your testing, ﴿by which You lead astray whom You will﴾, i.e., cause him to go astray, ﴿and guide whom You will﴾, i.e., guide him. ﴿You are our Protector﴾, i.e., the one who manages our affairs.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 156:

﴿And prescribe﴾ (i.e., make obligatory) ﴿for us in this world good, and in the Hereafter﴾ good ﴿indeed we have turned﴾ (tubna, i.e., repented) ﴿to You." He said﴾ (exalted is He) ﴿"My punishment — I afflict with it whom I will﴾ (i.e., His punishing) ﴿and My mercy has encompassed﴾ (i.e., has overspread) ﴿all things﴾ in this world. ﴿So I will prescribe it﴾ in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 157:

﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet, the unlettered﴾ Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ by his name and attributes, ﴿who enjoins on them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things﴾ that were forbidden in their law, ﴿and makes unlawful for them the evil things﴾ such as carrion and the like, ﴿and relieves them of their burden﴾ meaning their hardship, ﴿and the shackles﴾ meaning the severe restrictions ﴿that were upon them﴾, such as killing oneself as a means of repentance, and cutting off the place of impurity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, Qur'anic exegesis) on Surah 7, verse 158:

﴿Say﴾: an address to the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿O people, I am the Messenger of God to you all, the One to whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but He; He gives life and causes death. So believe in God and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, who believes in God and His words﴾ (i.e., the Qur'an), ﴿and follow him so that you may be guided﴾, i.e., ﴿you may be rightly guided﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 159:

﴿And among the people of Musa is a community﴾ (ummah), i.e., a group, ﴿who guide﴾ the people ﴿by the truth, and by it they act justly﴾ in judgment.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 7, verse 160:**

﴿And We divided them﴾: *faraqna* (We separated) the Children of Israel ﴿into twelve﴾, a *hal* (circumstantial accusative, *hal*) ﴿tribes﴾, a *badal* (substitution, *badal*) from it, meaning clans, ﴿nations﴾, a *badal* from what precedes it. ﴿And We revealed to Musa, when his people asked him for water﴾ in the *tih* (wandering, *tih*), ﴿that you strike the rock with your staff﴾, so he struck it, ﴿and there gushed forth﴾, that is, *infajarat* (burst forth), ﴿from it twelve springs﴾, corresponding to the number of the tribes, ﴿every people knew its drinking place﴾, each tribe from among them. ﴿And We shaded them with the clouds﴾ during the *tih*, from the heat of the sun. ﴿And We sent down upon them manna and quails﴾: they are the *taranjabin* (a sweet, honey-like substance) and the *tayr al-sumani* (quail), with the *mim* of *al-mann* pronounced with a light stress and the *qasr* (short vowel form) of *al-salwa*. ﴿And We said to them﴾

﴿And﴾ recall ﴿when it was said to them: "Dwell in this town"﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), ﴿and eat from it wherever you wish, and say﴾, meaning our command, ﴿"Ḥiṭṭah"﴾, ﴿and enter the gate﴾, meaning the gate of the town, ﴿prostrating﴾, meaning a prostration of bowing (sujud inḥina', a prostration of inclination). ﴿We will forgive﴾ is read with the nūn and with the tā', in the passive form (mabniyyan lil-maf'ūl, "built for the object"), ﴿your sins for you. We will increase [reward for] the good-doers﴾, meaning those who do good through obedience, with reward.

﴿So those among them who did wrong substituted a word other than the one that had been said to them﴾. They said: "A grain in a hair," and they entered crawling on their backsides. ﴿So We sent upon them a punishment from heaven﴾, a torment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 163:

﴿And ask them﴾, O Muhammad, as a rebuke, ﴿about the town that was by the sea﴾, neighbouring the Sea of Qulzum (the Red Sea), and it is Aylah, ﴿what happened to its people﴾, ﴿when they transgressed concerning the Sabbath﴾, by hunting fish, which they had been commanded to leave alone on it, ﴿when﴾ is an adverbial clause modifying ﴿they transgressed﴾, ﴿their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly﴾, visible upon the water, ﴿and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath﴾, meaning, on all other days, they did not honour the Sabbath, ﴿they did not come to them﴾, as a trial from Allah, ﴿thus We tested them for what they used to defiantly disobey﴾. When they hunted the fish, the town split into three groups: one group hunted with them, one group forbade them, and one group abstained from both the hunting and the forbidding.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 164:

﴿And when﴾ is coordinated with the preceding ﴿when﴾. ﴿A community among them said﴾: "Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?" They said: ﴿Our admonition is an excuse﴾, [a means of] excusing ourselves ﴿before your Lord﴾, lest we be blamed for negligence in abandoning the forbidding. ﴿And perhaps they will fear God﴾ [by refraining from] the hunting.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 7, verse 165:

﴿So when they forgot﴾ abandoned ﴿what they had been reminded of﴾ admonished ﴿with it﴾ and did not return, ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾ ﴿and seized those who did wrong﴾ by transgressing ﴿with a severe punishment﴾ intense.

﴿When they became arrogant﴾ (تَكَبَّرُوا) ﴿in refusing﴾ (تَرْك) ﴿what they had been forbidden, We said to them: "Be apes, despised and driven away."﴾ (صاغِرِينَ) So they became that. This is an explanation of what came before it. Ibn ʿAbbas (ibn ʿAbbās) said: "I do not know what was done to the group that remained silent." ʿIkrimah said: "They were not destroyed, because they disliked what the others had done and said: 'Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?' etc." Al-Ḥākim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he (Ibn ʿAbbas) returned to this view and was pleased with it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 167:

﴿And when your Lord declared﴾ (announced, a‘lama) ﴿that He would surely send against them﴾, i.e., the Jews, ﴿until the Day of Resurrection, those who would inflict upon them the worst torment﴾ through humiliation and the imposition of the jizyah (poll tax). So He sent against them Sulayman (Solomon), and after him Bukhtansar (Nebuchadnezzar), who killed them, took them captive, and imposed the jizyah upon them. They continued to pay it to the Magians, until Our Prophet ﷺ was sent and imposed it upon them. ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment﴾ for whoever disobeys Him, ﴿and indeed He is Forgiving﴾ to the people of His obedience, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them.

﴿وقَطَّعْناهُمْ﴾ means We separated them, ﴿فِي الأَرْض أُمَمًا﴾ means into communities, i.e. groups. ﴿مِنهُمْ الصّالِحُونَ ومِنهُمْ﴾ means among them are the righteous, and among them are some people ﴿دُون ذَلِكَ﴾, meaning the disbelievers and the defiantly disobedient. ﴿وبَلَوْناهُمْ بِالحَسَناتِ﴾ means We tested them with blessings, ﴿والسَّيِّئات﴾ means and with calamities, ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ meaning so that they might return from their defiance.

﴿So there succeeded them a successor who inherited the Book﴾, [the Torah] from their fathers, ﴿taking the goods of this lowly world﴾, i.e., the trash of this base thing, the world, whether lawful or unlawful. ﴿And they say: "It will be forgiven us"﴾ for what we did. ﴿And if goods like it come to them, they take it.﴾ The sentence is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: they hope for forgiveness while they return to what they did, persisting in it. And there is no promise of forgiveness in the Torah for persistence in sin.

﴿Has not the covenant of the Book been taken from them?﴾ This is an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr). The construct (iḍāfa) here carries the sense of "in," meaning the covenant concerning the Book. ﴿That they should not say about Allah except the truth, and they studied what is in it﴾ is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with "has been taken," meaning: they read what is in it. ﴿So why did they lie about Him?﴾ By attributing forgiveness to Him despite their persistence.

﴿And the Last Abode is better for those who are mindful﴾, i.e., who avoid the unlawful. ﴿Will they not understand?﴾ (read with the letter yā' or tā') that it is better, so that they would prefer it over the world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 170:

﴿Those who hold fast to the Book﴾ (read with both the doubled and the single letter, yumassikūna and yumsikūna) from among them, ﴿and establish prayer﴾, like ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions, ﴿indeed We do not waste the reward of the reformers﴾. The sentence is the predicate of ﴿those who﴾, and in it the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun, i.e. "their reward."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 171:

﴿And﴾ remember ﴿when We raised the mountain﴾, We lifted it up from its base, ﴿above them as though it were a canopy﴾, ﴿and they thought﴾, i.e. were certain, ﴿that it was going to fall upon them﴾, i.e. fall on them, because of God's promise to them that it would fall if they did not accept the rulings of the Torah. They had been prostrating (ʾabwāhā) for its weight, so they accepted. And We said to them: ﴿Take what We have given you with strength﴾, i.e. with determination and diligence, ﴿and remember what is in it﴾, i.e. by acting upon it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 172:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when﴾ (idh) [the time when] ﴿your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾ — a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimal) from what precedes it, with the preposition repeated — ﴿by bringing forth some of them from the loins of others, from the loins of Adam, generation after generation, as ants (kal-dharr) are born one from another, at Nu'man on the Day of 'Arafah. He set up for them proofs of His lordship and endowed them with reason﴾ — ﴿and He made them bear witness against themselves﴾, saying: ﴿"Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes! We bear witness"﴾ — You are our Lord — ﴿that﴾ (an) ﴿they should not say﴾ (yaqulu, with the ya' and the ta' in both places) ﴿on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this"﴾ — i.e., the disbelievers — ﴿of this﴾ tawhid, ﴿not knowing it﴾.

Or [lest] you should say, "Our fathers before us ascribed partners to God, and we were offspring after them, so will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"

﴿أوْ تَقُولُوا إنّما أشْرَكَ آباؤُنا مِن قَبْل﴾: [meaning] before us. ﴿وكُنّا ذُرِّيَّة مِن بَعْدهمْ﴾: and we were offspring after them, so we followed them. ﴿أفَتُهْلِكنا﴾: will You punish us. ﴿بِما فَعَلَ المُبْطِلُونَ﴾: for what the falsifiers, our fathers, did by establishing polytheism.

The meaning is that they cannot plead this, since they bore witness against themselves to monotheism, and the reminder of it through the mouth of the bearer of the miracle (the Prophet ﷺ) stands in place of its being recalled in their souls.

And thus do We detail the verses (﴿وكَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّل الآيات﴾), explaining them, just as We explained the covenant (al-mithaq), so that they may reflect upon them (﴿لِيَتَدَبَّرُوها﴾) and perhaps they will return (﴿ولَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾) from their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 175:

﴿Recite﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿to them﴾, i.e., the Jews, ﴿the news of him to whom We gave Our verses, but he detached himself from them﴾, i.e., he went out in his disbelief as a snake comes out of its skin. He was Bal'am ibn Ba'ura' (Bal'am son of Ba'ura'), one of the scholars of the Children of Israel. He was asked to invoke (a curse) upon Musa (Moses), and a gift was offered to him, so he invoked, and it turned back upon him, and his tongue hung out upon his chest. ﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, i.e., overtook him, and he became his companion.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 7, Verse 176**

﴿Had We willed, We would have raised him thereby﴾ to the ranks of the scholars, ﴿thereby﴾, by enabling him to act upon it. ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾ settled upon it, meaning the worldly life, and inclined to it, ﴿and followed his desire﴾ in calling himself to it. So We abased him. ﴿So his likeness﴾ his description ﴿is that of the dog: if you drive it away﴾ by chasing and scolding it ﴿it pants﴾ lolling out its tongue, ﴿or﴾ if ﴿you leave it, it pants﴾. No other animal is like this. The two conditional clauses are in the accusative of circumstance (ḥāl), meaning panting and abased in every state. The intended point is the comparison in lowliness and baseness, indicated by the particle الفاء (al-fā’), which signals that what follows it is the result of what precedes it: inclining to the worldly life and following desire. This is further indicated by His saying ﴿That is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the narratives﴾ to the Jews, ﴿that perhaps they may reflect﴾ ponder upon them, ﴿and thus believe﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 7, verse 177:

﴿Evil is﴾ (بِئْسَ, bi'sa, "evil is/how wretched is") ﴿the example of the people﴾ (أيْ مَثَل القَوْم, i.e., the example of the people) ﴿who denied Our signs and were wronging themselves﴾ (كانُوا يَظْلِمُونَ, "were wronging") by the denial.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 179:

﴿And We have certainly created⦗dhara'na⦘﴾ — "khalaqna" (We created) — ﴿for Hell many of the jinn and mankind; they have hearts with which they do not understand⦗yafqahuna⦘ bihā﴾ — "al-haqq" (the truth) — ﴿and they have eyes with which they do not see⦗yubsirun⦘ bihā﴾ — "dalā'il qudrat Allāh" (the signs of God's power), "baṣar i'tibār" (the sight of reflection) — ﴿and they have ears with which they do not hear⦗yasma'un⦘ bihā﴾ — "al-āyāt wa'l-mawā'iz" (the verses and admonitions), "samā' tadabbur wa'ttiʿāẓ" (hearing of reflection and taking heed) — ﴿those are like cattle⦗al-an'ām⦘﴾ — "fī 'adam al-fiqh wa'l-baṣar wa'l-istimā'" (in lacking understanding, sight and hearing) — ﴿rather, they are more astray⦗aḍall⦘﴾ — "min al-an'ām" (than cattle), "li-annahā taṭlub manāfi'hā wa-tahrub min maḍārrihā wa-hā'ulā'i yaqdumūna 'alā al-nār mu'ānadah" (because cattle seek their benefits and flee their harms, whereas these rush into the Fire out of obstinate opposition).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 180:

﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful Names, so call upon Him by them.﴾ They are ninety-nine, as the hadith concerning them has reported. Al-husna (the most beautiful) is the feminine form of al-ahsan (the most beautiful). ﴿So call upon Him by them.﴾ Name Him by them. ﴿And leave﴾ abandon ﴿those who deviate﴾ from the verb alhada and lahada (to deviate), meaning they turn away from the truth. ﴿concerning His Names﴾ by deriving from them names for their deities: such as al-Lat from Allah, al-Uzza from al-Aziz (the Mighty), and Manat from al-Mannan (the Bestower). ﴿They will be recompensed﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿for what they used to do.﴾ This was before the command to fight.
And among those whom We created is a community that guides by the truth and by it acts justly. They are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), as in the ḥadīth (prophetic tradition).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 182:

﴿And those who denied Our signs﴾ — the Qur'an — from among the people of Mecca. ﴿We will lead them step by step﴾ — We will seize them gradually, little by little.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 183:

﴿And I give them respite﴾ I grant them time. ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾ strong, unbearable.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 184:

﴿Have they not reflected?﴾ So that they would know ﴿that there is no madness in their companion﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿and he is only a clear warner.﴾ Clear in warning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 185:

﴿Have they not considered the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth, and what things Allah has created?﴾ The dominion (mulk) of the heavens and the earth, and in ﴿what Allah has created of things﴾, is an explanation of what they should reflect upon, so that they may infer from it the power of its Creator and His oneness. And in ﴿that﴾, meaning that ﴿perhaps their term has drawn near﴾, has approached (qad iqtaraba), ﴿their appointed time﴾, so that they die as disbelievers and go to the Fire; so let them hasten to faith. ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾, meaning the Qur'an.

﴿Whoever Allah leads astray, there is none to guide him. And He leaves them﴾ (read with the *yāʾ* and with the *nūn*, *wayadharuhum* and *wanadharuhum*), with *rafʿ* (nominative) as a resumptive clause (*istiʾnāfan*, a new sentence that begins afresh), and with *jazm* (jussive) as a conjunction (*ʿaṭfan*) upon the position (*maḥall*) of what follows the *fāʾ*. ﴿In their transgression they wander bewildered﴾, moving back and forth in confusion (*taḥayyuran*).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 187:

﴿They ask you﴾ i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿about the Hour﴾ the Resurrection, ﴿when will be its arrival﴾ when it will happen. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal it at its time﴾ none will manifest it at its time; the lam here carries the sense of fi (in). ﴿Except Him. It is heavy﴾ it is great, ﴿in the heavens and the earth﴾ upon their inhabitants, because of its terror. ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly﴾ unexpectedly. ﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed﴾ one who presses hard in asking ﴿about it﴾ until you have known it. ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with Allah﴾ (emphasis). ﴿But most people do not know﴾ that its knowledge is with Him, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 188:

﴿Say: I possess no power to bring benefit to myself﴾ (ajlubuhu, i.e., to bring it) ﴿nor harm﴾ (udfa'uhu, i.e., to ward it off) ﴿except what God wills. And had I known the unseen﴾ (ma ghaaba 'anni, i.e., what was hidden from me) ﴿I would have acquired abundant good﴾ ﴿and no evil would have touched me﴾ (of poverty or otherwise, because I would have guarded against it by avoiding harmful things) ﴿I am only a warner﴾ (in-, i.e., mA, "not") ﴿I am only a warner﴾ of the Fire to those who disbelieve ﴿and a bringer of good tidings﴾ of Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 189:

﴿He﴾ i.e., Allah, ﴿who created you from a single soul﴾ i.e., Adam, ﴿and made from it its mate﴾ created from it its spouse, Hawwa' (Eve), ﴿that he might find rest in her﴾ and be at ease with her, ﴿and when he covered her﴾ had intercourse with her, ﴿she bore a light burden﴾ which was the sperm-drop, ﴿and she went about with it﴾ she went about and came and went, because of its lightness, ﴿but when she became heavy﴾ with the largeness of the child in her womb, and they feared that it would be an animal, ﴿they called upon Allah, their Lord: "If You give us a righteous one﴾ a child who is sound, ﴿we will surely be among the thankful"﴾ to You for it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 7, verse 190:**

﴿When He gave them a righteous child,﴾ they ascribed to Him partners ﴿in what He had given them.﴾ In another reading, *shirkan* is read with a kasra on the *shin* and with tanwin, meaning a partner (*sharīkan*), ﴿in what He had given them,﴾ by naming him ʿAbd al-Ḥārith. It is not fitting that he be named a slave (*ʿabd*) except to Allah. This is not an association (*shirk*) in servitude, because of Adam's protection (*ʿiṣmah*, freedom from sin). Samurah reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When Hawwa' gave birth, Iblis came to her. None of her children had survived, so he said: 'Name him ʿAbd al-Ḥārith, for he will survive.' She named him so, and he survived. That was from the inspiration and command of Satan." Narrated by al-Ḥākim, who said it is *ṣaḥīḥ* (authentic), and by al-Tirmidhī, who said it is *ḥasan gharīb* (good, strange). ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ That is, the people of Makkah associate with Him the idols. The sentence (*jumlah*) is a causal clause (*jumlah musabbabah*), coordinated (*ʿaṭf*) upon *khalaqakum* (﴿He created you﴾), and what lies between them is a parenthetical interjection (*iʿtirāḍ*).
﴿Do they associate with Him⁠﴾ in worship

﴿And they are not able to give them (their worshippers) any help,﴾ ﴿nor can they help themselves,﴾ by preventing from themselves whoever intends them harm, whether by breaking them or otherwise. The interrogative form is for rebuke.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 193:

﴿And if you call them﴾ i.e., the idols, ﴿to guidance, they will not follow you.﴾ [It is read] with light and with heavy (tashdid) pronunciation of the taa' [i.e., yattabi'uukum or yattabi'uukum with tashdid, both readings]. ﴿It is all the same for you whether you call them or you are silent﴾ concerning their call; ﴿they will not follow it, because they do not hear.﴾

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 7, verse 194:

﴿Indeed, those whom you invoke﴾ (i.e., worship) ﴿besides Allah are servants (ʿibād) like you, owned (mamlūka)﴾ ﴿so call upon them, and let them respond to you﴾ (to your supplication) ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in claiming that they are gods. Then he (Allah) explained the extent of their incapacity and the superiority of their worshippers over them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 195:

﴿Do they have feet with which they walk, or do they have hands with which they grasp?﴾ "Aydin" is the plural of "yad" (hand), in an interrogative of denial, meaning: they have none of these things that belong to you. So how can you worship them, when you are better off than they are? ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad: ﴿Call upon your partners﴾ to destroy me, ﴿then plot against me and give me no respite﴾, that is, do not give me a delay. For I do not care about you.
Indeed, my Protector (walī, i.e. the one who manages my affairs) is Allah, ﴿who has sent down the Book﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿and He takes care of the righteous﴾ by protecting them.
﴿Those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾ So how could I care about them?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 198:

﴿And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear; and you see them looking at you﴾ — i.e., the idols — ﴿O Muhammad﴾ — i.e., the idols — ﴿looking at you﴾ — i.e., they face you like one who looks.

﴿Take forgiveness﴾: ease (al-yusr) from the characters of people, and do not search for it. ﴿And enjoin what is known (al-ma'ruf)﴾: with the known (bil-ma'ruf). ﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾: so do not retaliate against them for their foolishness.

﴿And if﴾ in it there is *idghām* (assimilation, the merging of one sound into another) of the *nūn* of *in* (إنْ), the conditional particle, into *mā*, the added particle (مَزِيدَة). ﴿an incitement from Satan incites you﴾, that is, if a diverter diverts you from what you have been commanded. ﴿Then seek refuge in Allah﴾: this is the *jawāb al-sharṭ* (the response of the conditional clause), and the response of the imperative is omitted, that is, He will repel it from you. ﴿Indeed He is All-Hearing﴾ of the speech, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of the deed.

﴿Indeed, those who are mindful of God, when a visitation﴾ struck them, ﴿طَيْف (ṭayf)﴾, and in another reading (qirāʾa, a variant recitation) ﴿طائِف (ṭāʾif)﴾, meaning something that befell them, ﴿from Satan, they remember﴾ God's punishment and His reward, ﴿and then they are seeing clearly﴾ the truth apart from anything else, ﴿so they turn back﴾.

﴿And their brothers﴾, i.e., the brothers of the devils from among the disbelievers, ﴿extend them﴾, i.e., the devils, ﴿in error. Then﴾ they ﴿do not refrain﴾, i.e., they do not desist from it through insight, as the God-fearing ones gained insight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 203:

﴿And when you do not bring them a sign﴾ — i.e., the people of Makkah — ﴿of what they proposed﴾ — ﴿they say: "Why do you not invent it?"﴾ — i.e., "Why do you not create it" (ijtabaytaha) from yourself? ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord."﴾ And it is not for me to bring anything from myself. ﴿This﴾ Qur'an is ﴿insights﴾ — proofs (hujaj).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 204:

﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent﴾ (from speech) ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾. It was revealed concerning abandoning speech during the khutbah (sermon), and He expressed it by "the Qur'an" because the khutbah includes it. It was also said that it refers to the recitation of the Qur'an in general.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 205:

﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾, i.e., secretly, ﴿humbly﴾, submissively, ﴿and fearfully﴾, out of fear of Him, ﴿and without loudness in speech﴾, i.e., intermediate between the secret and the loud, ﴿in the mornings and the evenings﴾, the beginnings and ends of the day, ﴿and do not be among the heedless﴾, of the remembrance of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 7, verse 206:

﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ — i.e., the angels — ﴿do not feel too proud to worship Him﴾ — they do not act arrogantly toward His worship — ﴿and they exalt Him﴾ — they declare Him free of what is not fitting for Him — ﴿and to Him they prostrate﴾ — i.e., they single Him out with humility and worship, so be like them.
